summary: SQL, Tableau, KPIs, A/B testing, stakeholders

paragraphs: I'm applying for the Data Analyst role on the Commercial Insights team at Acme Analytics. The work you describe, turning sales and customer data into dashboards that commercial leaders act on, is the work I do every day at Northwind Retail, and the part I enjoy most.

At Northwind I built 12 Tableau and Power BI dashboards for store operations and merchandising, and about 80 people use them every week. Before that, most of those numbers lived in manual Excel reports. Rewriting them as SQL on Snowflake cut our weekly reporting from 6 hours to 1, and it gave category managers one set of KPIs (sell-through, stock-outs, basket size) that we defined together.

I also like testing ideas properly. With our marketing team I designed and analyzed A/B tests on email promotions and reported lift with confidence intervals, so decisions came from evidence rather than the loudest opinion. To keep reports trustworthy, I wrote a daily Python check that flags missing store feeds before anything goes out.

Your posting mentions pricing and promotion tests and stronger data quality checks in your pipelines. Those are the two areas where I think I can help Acme Analytics fastest. I haven't used Looker in production yet; I have built the same kind of semantic layer in Tableau and would ramp up on it quickly.
Thank you for your time and consideration. I would be glad to walk you through one of my dashboards.

fields.Main Strengths: SQL + Tableau daily; KPI definition; A/B tests
fields.Resume Strategy: Lead with dashboards and SQL automation; A/B tests second; honest Looker gap in the letter.
